title: The Future of Evals: From LLM as a Judge to Agent as a Judge — Aparna Dhinakaran, Arize AI
talk_summary: Arize argues that fixed LLM-as-judge rubrics miss failures in long-horizon agent trajectories, so teams should add an agent-as-judge that reads traces, discovers patterns, and can file fixes. The talk is mostly a product pitch for Arize Signal, with no measured defect-rate results.

takeaways.what_they_do: A long-running eval agent reads agent traces, discovers issue patterns, and does adaptive analysis instead of fixed rubric scoring.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Signal's actually a long-running agent that can read traces sent in, discover patterns of issues.
takeaways.numbers: 100M evals/month; avg 12 eval jobs; top teams >3,800 evaluators

takeaways.what_they_do: Keep deterministic checks and LLM judges for known rubrics, add an agent judge for open-ended trajectories.
takeaways.evidence_quote: most teams today are doing the first two, but the future of evals is actually having all three.

takeaways.what_they_do: Agent judge inspects the full trace for repeated tool calls, loops, and inefficient paths that final-output judges miss.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it was calling the same tool for repeatedly long time, the trajectory was inefficient.

takeaways.what_they_do: Because the eval agent has trace analysis, it can open a PR with a fix for discovered failure patterns.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it can go put up a PR and put up a fix.

takeaways.what_they_do: Use a long-running eval agent to mine traces and discover issue patterns, generating concrete work items.
takeaways.evidence_quote: read traces sent in, discover patterns of issues.

takeaways.technique: Detect context loss and done-state failures
takeaways.what_they_do: Agent judge can catch context forgetting, not knowing when done, and loops in long-horizon agents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It would forget context. It wouldn't know when something was done.
